perf.summary: Replace the inner mex linear scan with trailing-zero-count of the complemented 64-bit mask.
perf.currentCost: `int g = 0; while ((seen & (1L << g)) != 0) g++;` is a serial, data-dependent loop run once per i (n times), up to 64 iterations each with a branch and 64-bit shift. This dominates the per-cell cost for dense reachability sets.
perf.proposedChange: Use `int g = math.tzcnt(~(ulong)seen);` (or `BitOperations.TrailingZeroCount((ulong)(~seen))`). This returns the smallest g with bit g unset, i.e. the mex, in one instruction.
perf.rationale: Collapses an O(mex) per-cell loop into O(1) branchless tzcnt; removes mispredicted branches and the serial shift chain in the hot DP loop. Burst vectorizes/lowers tzcnt natively.
perf.risk: If all 64 bits of seen are set, ~seen==0 and tzcnt(0)==64; the original loop would shift `1L << 64` which is undefined/UB (shift count masked to 0 in C#), so the original is already broken for the all-bits-set case. The proposed version returns 64 deterministically, which is strictly more correct; for all valid inputs (mex < 64) behavior is identical. Cast to ulong to avoid sign-extension of the complement.
